R6F-grouse-atv-0003.name: 3.5 km S of Cheslatta Lake
R6F-grouse-atv-0003.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R6F-grouse-atv-0003.parkWhat: where the truck road ends (Marilla FSR); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle)

evidence.t: 100% of the stretch in grouse forest zones (BWBS, CWH, ESSF, ICH, IDF, MS, SBPS, SBS).
14 cutblocks touch the road (30 years old or less): edges and clover.
2 wetlands, lakes or creeks along the road: riparian edges.

seasonRows.notes: No row in the Region 6 table (pages 50 and 51), so no general open season (page 5: open seasons are only those in the synopsis).

plan: Drive: from Village of Burns Lake, about 69 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Tibbets Creek Rd, Hwy 16, Hwy 35, Brown Rd.
Park: 53.70322, -125.40066, where the truck road ends (Marilla FSR); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle). Map links below.
Walk 180 m to the start. Ride: the unnamed road stretch, 3.5 km one way. About 71 min one way at 3 km/h.
Hunt: grouse, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Walk slowly in the first and last 2 hours of light. Watch where cutblocks and creeks meet the road (Tip).
Use: .22 rimfire for a sitting grouse inside 25 m (27 yd), or a shotgun with lead 6 or 7.5 (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 6-4, Region 6. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-02, closures 2026-10-16.
R6F-grouse-atv-0003.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 6-4: about 7,565 hunter days a year for all big game (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.83 days per square km, middle third of BC MUs; access: average access. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Good solo
tags.why: Short pack out: 0.2 km and about 0 m of climb from the parking (Tip). Cell coverage is not in the data: leave a trip plan and carry SOS or a satellite messenger (lesson: Bush safety).

Black bear: young cutblocks and burns grow berries in late summer and fall (Tip).

plan: Drive: from Village of Burns Lake, about 91 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 53.57105, -125.24986, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 1.8 km N, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 201 m, about 55 min at 3 km/h.
Hunt: moose, season: VERIFY. Glass the wetland and cutblock edges at dawn and dusk. Move slowly, stop often (Tip). Also: black bear (see evidence).
Use: .308 Winchester, 165 to 180 grain premium bullet, shots inside about 200 m (219 yd) (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 6-4, Region 6. Season: no general open season (synopsis page 50, 95%). 1 legal flag below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-02, closures 2026-10-16.
R6F-moose-walk-0005.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 6-4: about 1,452 hunter days a year for moose (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.16 days per square km, middle third of BC MUs; access: average access. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Beginner friendly
tags.why: Quieter spot only 1.8 km from the parking: fewer hunters, short walk back (Tip, estimate).

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).
